triples.subject: ArtificialIntelligence
triples.context: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has already transformed healthcare and continues to hold substantial potential for further inno-vation within clinical ecosystems.

triples.subject: MedicalLargeVisionLanguageModel
triples.context: Recently, Medical Large Vision-Language Models (Med-LVLMs) have shown great promise for advancing interactive and intelligent diagnosis [1, 2].

triples.subject: MedicalLargeVisionLanguageModel
triples.context: Despite this potential, current Med-LVLMs still face sig-nificant reliability issues, particularly their tendency to gen-erate non-factual medical responses [3], making them unreli-able in critical medical applications.

triples.subject: MedicalLargeVisionLanguageModel

triples.subject: DiagnosticError
triples.context: These factuality issues raise serious concerns when deploying such models in clini-cal settings, where even small diagnostic errors could lead to severe consequences for patient care.

triples.subject: FineTuning
triples.context: Recently, researchers have begun to focus on improving the factuality of Med-LVLMs through various techniques, in-cluding fine-tuning [1], low-rank adaptation [4], and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) [5, 6].

triples.subject: RetrievalAugmentedGeneration
triples.context: Recently, researchers have begun to focus on improving the factuality of Med-LVLMs through various techniques, in-cluding fine-tuning [1], low-rank adaptation [4], and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) [5, 6].

triples.subject: FineTuning
triples.context: Fine-tuning is a direct method to improve model performance, but faces several lim-itations in the medical field.

triples.subject: MedicalDomain
triples.context: First, there is a lack of sufficient high-quality labeled data for fine-tuning in the medical do-main.

triples.subject: DistributionShift
triples.context: Second, a distribution shift often exists between train-ing datasets the real-world deployment data, leading to signif-icantly worse model performance during deployment.

triples.subject: RetrievalAugmentedGeneration
triples.context: Hence, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) [5] has emerged as a promising solution, grounding model outputs in external knowledge to improve factuality.

triples.subject: framework_medrag
triples.context: Recent works adapted RAG for medicine, including MedRAG [6], MMed-RAG [7].

triples.subject: CausalityBasedMethod
triples.context: Causality-based methods seek to improve retrieval accu-racy and representation learning, but critical limitations per-sist [8].

triples.subject: framework_causalrag
triples.context: CausalRAG [9] ranks contexts by causal importance, but does not address cross-modal alignment.

triples.subject: framework_cmcrl
triples.context: Similarly, CM-CRL [10] learns shared causal representations but underuses the structural dependencies needed for medical reasoning.

triples.subject: CausalGraph
triples.context: Al-though causal graphs improve interpretability [11, 12], cur-rent approaches mainly rely on language-only causal discov-ery [9].

triples.subject: ExplicitCausalGraph
triples.context: Ac-cordingly, we propose to build explicit causal graphs from multimodal data and use them to guide RAG retrieval for medical reasoning.

triples.subject: framework_mcrag
triples.context: In this paper, we propose MCRAG (Multimodal Causal Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a retrieval framework de-signed to improve factuality and robustness in Med-LVLMs.

triples.subject: framework_mcrag
triples.context: MCRAG introduces a causal alignment graph constructed from verifiable medical literature, capturing structured depen-dencies between visual and textual modalities.

triples.subject: McragFramework
triples.context: In this section, we presentMCRAG—a multi-modal, causal retrieval-augmented generation framework that improves the factuality of Med-LVLMs by tightly coupling retrieval with an explicit Structural Causal Model (SCM).

triples.subject: McragFramework
triples.context: In this section, we presentMCRAG—a multi-modal, causal retrieval-augmented generation framework that improves the factuality of Med-LVLMs by tightly coupling retrieval with an explicit Structural Causal Model (SCM).

triples.subject: McragFramework
triples.context: The framework has three stages: (1)domain-aware retrieval, which selects the optimal retriever for each input; (2)adaptive context se- lection, which filters and sizes evidence on the fly; and (3)RAG-based preference fine-tuning, which aligns responses with SCM-supported evidence.
